unit: per job: one PCV (positive crankcase ventilation) valve, fitted, with its grommet or hose only where sold with it; diagnosis not included. This covers engines where the valve is a separate part. On some engines the PCV valve or orifice is built into the valve cover, the intake manifold or an oil separator and is not sold alone; that is a different, larger job and is not priced here

finding: There is no live range for this job on the site today (live is null), so this is a first build, and it could not be completed: this file is held. What the evidence shows: where the PCV valve is a separate part it is cheap and quick. The genuine valve lists at $8.77 for a 2017 Impreza and $56.05 for a 2016 Ram 1500 3.6L ($93.75 for the 5.7L), and the stated times found run from about 10 minutes to 1 hour. Built totals (parts + stated hours x $120-$160/hr, the national middle labor rate used for these checks) can only be given at the top end: truck 2016 Ram 1500 3.6L up to about $216 (genuine valve, 1.0 hr); economy 2017 Impreza up to about $89 (genuine valve, 0.5 hr). The low ends cannot be built because no aftermarket valve was verified, on a page stating the part is new, as fitting either example; the truck's labor low is a seller's 10-minute figure (0.17 hr, about $20 of labor), which is less than any shop bills. No totals can be built for midsize or luxury: no parts price was loaded for either example. The benchmarks sit at $76-$220 (RepairPal $124-$173, AutoNation Mobile Service $80-$220, FIXD $76-$92), mostly labor, which fits a shop's minimum charge of half an hour to an hour plus a small part. A supportable working range for a separate, reachable valve is roughly $75-$220; that is drawn from the benchmarks and the top-end builds, not from a full build. How solid the labor times are: weak. No maker-stated time for replacing only the valve, printed with a unit, was found for any class. Subaru prints 0.2 for 'PCV VALVE R&R' on the 2017-2018 Impreza and 0.3 for valve and hose with inspection, but with no unit, so both are cross-checks. Nissan's Sentra bulletin implies 0.1 hr (0.5 hrs with the valve against 0.4 hrs without), Hyundai's Sonata 2.5T time (1.0 M/H) includes cleaning the intake, and FCA's Grand Wagoneer times (0.3-0.5 Hrs.) include a ventilation test. The truck figures are a parts seller's approximate install times, 10 minutes for the example and 1 hour for a 2003-2008 5.7L. The 0.5 hr high used for the other three classes is one parts retailer's do-it-yourself guide. No stated time was found for an engine whose valve sits under the intake manifold, which is the long version of this job; RepairPal's 'an hour or two' and AutoNation Mobile Service's '1 to 2 hours' are the only signs of it and are other estimators' figures, so they are not used. Engines with the valve built into the valve cover or an oil separator (a parts guide notes some GM engines have the orifice built into the rocker cover; on Volkswagen's turbo four the unit is quoted at $78-$140) are outside this unit. HELD because: (1) no class has a verified aftermarket price, and midsize and luxury have no parts price at all; (2) three classes have no labor low and no vehicle-specific range end; (3) no stated time covers the under-manifold case. To finish: choose midsize and luxury examples with a separate valve and a priced catalog page, load a new aftermarket valve for each class, and find a maker time printed with a unit (Nissan and FCA print units; Subaru and GM often do not) or a trade-press book time, including one for an under-manifold valve. This is an estimate, never a quote and never a diagnosis.
extras: A quote often adds diagnosis, a new grommet or PCV hose (Subaru says to replace the hose with the valve as a set), thread sealer where the valve screws into the engine, shop supplies and sales tax. Where the valve sits under the intake manifold, expect intake gaskets and more labor. Where it is built into the valve cover or an oil separator, the whole cover or separator is replaced instead, which is a different and dearer job. A valve that has failed can leave oil in the intake or air filter, and cleaning that is extra.
